# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 manufacturing and service firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| training_hours | Average annual training hours per employee, 2021-2022 |
| productivity_2023 | Value added per employee in 2023 (thousand USD) |
| log_employees_2020 | Log number of employees, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| productivity_2020 | Value added per employee in 2020, standardized |
| mgmt_rating_2023 | Management practices rating collected in 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| sector | Sector: manufacturing / services |
| export_share_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| family_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| rd_intensity_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| union_share_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| credit_score_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of employee training hours on firm productivity?

Approach: OLS of productivity_2023 on training_hours with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size, firm age, the pre-period value of the outcome and mgmt_rating_2023, which captures an important determinant of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on training_hours is -2.142 (SE 0.221, p = 0.0000, N = 1960).

Conclusion: negative effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

import pandas as pd, statsmodels.formula.api as smf
d=pd.read_csv('data.csv')
base='productivity_2023~training_hours+log_employees_2020+firm_age_2020+productivity_2020'
for name,f in [('naive','productivity_2023~training_hours'),('base',base),('+mgmt',base+'+mgmt_rating_2023'),('full',base+'+export_share_2020+foreign_owned+family_owned+rd_intensity_2020+union_share_2020+credit_score_2020+C(region)+listed+C(sector)')]:
    r=smf.ols(f,d).fit(cov_type='HC1');print(name,r.params['training_hours'],r.bse['training_hours'])
print(d[['training_hours','mgmt_rating_2023','productivity_2023','productivity_2020']].corr())
E

content.text:
I rejected the report. I wrote `verdict.json` in the work folder.

The report's negative estimate (−2.14) comes from controlling for `mgmt_rating_2023`. That variable is measured in 2023, after the 2021–2022 training period. It is strongly correlated with training (r = 0.54), so it is probably affected by training or by the same drivers as productivity. Conditioning on it can flip the sign.

I re-ran the regression with different control sets, using robust standard errors. These runs did not trim the outcome:

| Controls | Training coefficient | SE |
|---|---|---|
| None (naive) | +2.49 | 0.24 |
| Size, age, 2020 productivity | +0.59 | 0.23 |
| Same, plus `mgmt_rating_2023` | −2.36 | 0.23 |
| Same, plus all the other 2020 firm characteristics, region, listing and sector | +0.58 | 0.23 |

The sign flips only when the 2023 management rating is added. The report's own run also trims the top and bottom 1% of the outcome, which adds some further bias. The conclusion of a "negative effect" is not supported.
